Estimates for one receiver, using the current scene and average JPEG size. The last column uses 2× headroom as a planning guideline, not a guarantee or a measured network speed. More detail or motion can increase JPEG sizes. Two receivers need roughly twice the total bandwidth. These FPS rows are calculations, not camera mode choices.

Receiver feedback colors (recent 2 seconds):
Green: cycle at most 80% of a camera frame interval and under 2% skipped frames.
Orange: less headroom or 2–20% skipped.
Red: cycle over two frame intervals, at least 20% skipped, or a stalled transfer.
Gray: no receiver, not enough samples, or MJPEG without feedback.

The receiver cycle includes sending, decoding, drawing to the browser canvas and the reply. It does not measure exposure time or the delay of OBS output, your display or audio. Sent rate includes all receivers; MJPEG reports writes without playback confirmation.

For low delay in OBS:
1. Use Browser Source with %1$s. Set its width and height to the camera resolution and its FPS to 30.
2. Disable or close the old MJPEG source to avoid duplicate traffic.
3. If you keep Media Source with /cam.mjpeg, try Network Buffering = 0 MB; only raise it if reception becomes unstable.
4. Prefer a wired PC and strong 5/6 GHz Wi-Fi, or a wired phone connection. Internet upload speed is not the same as LAN capacity.

The /view receiver allows one frame in flight and one latest frame waiting. Slow reception skips stale frames; JPEG quality and resolution are unchanged. Extra buffering adds delay; it cannot repair a sustained bandwidth deficit.

For lip sync, record a clap test in OBS. If audio is consistently ahead of video, delay that audio by the measured difference using Sync Offset. A changing delay must be fixed at its source first.
RemoteCam needs the camera and, on Android 17, local network access. If permission was permanently denied, enable it in system app settings.
